The study retrieved 843 WoSCC candidates on 6 January 2024, screened titles and abstracts, and included 652 English articles and reviews from 2017–2023.
The corpus covers 168 sources, 2,654 authors, and 19,174 references, with 149.8% annual growth and 13.29 average citations per document.
The included document composition was 619 articles, 4 data papers, 13 proceedings papers, and 16 reviews.
Annual publications were 1, 1, 16, 48, 113, 230, and 243 from 2017 through 2023.
China produced 426 papers and the United States 142.
China and the United States had advantages in output and collaboration, but worldwide cooperation needs strengthening.

The leading cited papers and their global/local citation counts are those reported in Table 7.

rationale: B is the more complete synthesis for its paired corpus: it reports retrieval and screening, countries, institutions, journals, authors, cited works, keywords, cooperation, and challenges. A is cleaner and more reproducible, but includes a factual Bradford-method error and several unsupported phase and causal interpretations; B's main weakness is limited caution and occasional quality language.

claims.claim: The study screened 231 records, retained 220 after document-type exclusions, and included 219 English publications from 2015–2022.
The final corpus comprised 164 articles and 55 reviews after the non-English review was removed.
Publication volume fluctuated but generally increased, especially after 2019.
China, the United States, and Germany were leading contributors.
China led total citations and H-index, while South Korea led average citations.
A fitted curve projected approximately 300 annual articles by 2050.
The forecast establishes continued real-world growth to 2050.
Wang Y. and Zhang H. led author productivity with six publications each.
There were 141 core authors and the cooperation maps covered authors, countries, and institutions.
Citation-burst analysis identified Valadi H as strongest, followed by Thery, Raposo, Kowal, and Li.
There were 317 recurring keywords and seven named keyword clusters.
Expression, cells, Cas9, and RNA were the most frequent listed keywords.
Gene therapy and nanovesicles were enduring concepts, while genome, protein delivery, and plasma were emerging.
The study was the first bibliometric analysis of the topic.
Citation counts reflect publication quality or author research value.
The extracted report covers trends, countries, citations, authors, cooperation, citation bursts, journals, and keyword evolution, but provides limited source, parameter, and forecast caution.
The corpus contains 259 unique works from 2015–2022, exhaustively retrieved and deduplicated.
The stated metadata completeness percentages are correct.
Output peaked at 72 in 2022, endpoint CAGR was 66.85%, and 2021 was the only annual decline.
International Journal of Molecular Sciences, Xiaohui Chen, and Harvard University lead source, author, and institution productivity.
Harvard, Peking, and Sun Yat-sen Universities tie at seven publications.
Zone 1 has 23 sources and 85 documents.
Mean citations are 72.09, median 32.00, maximum 1,436, and 35 works are uncited.
The most-cited work is the Pseudomonas review and appears tangential to the intended intersection.
The keyword and four other network sizes, clusters, and principal mapped nodes are as reported.
The evidence establishes a trans-Pacific institutional axis and strong national clustering.
The thematic structure is dominated by therapeutic EV–CRISPR delivery.
The report explicitly limits interpretation by source coverage, citation windows, metadata, abstract-only evidence, network parameterization, and productivity-quality distinctions.

rationale: B is more reproducible, structured, and cautious, and it identifies a likely search-strategy outlier instead of treating every retrieved record as substantively central. A has valuable country and burst analyses, but its unsupported priority claim, quality interpretations, and long-range extrapolation reduce evidence-bounded usefulness.
